title: Chat is the agent now — and What's New becomes a release history
summary: The native Chat screen becomes the default for every Claude session, on new installs and existing ones alike; the embedded terminal stays as Terminal (legacy), one dropdown away in Settings → Agents. What's New is now one page per release, led by its version number and built from real screenshots of the app.

title: Your agent, as an app — the in-app agent is no longer a terminal
summary: The Chat view renders the same Claude Code engine as native app UI instead of scrollback: permission asks, questions, sub-agent groups, diffs and images each become a card you can act on. Chat and terminal resume the same conversation both ways.

title: The brain starts forming opinions — falsifiable theses, re-tested every sleep cycle
summary: The proactive learning layer lands: claims your project makes about itself, with predictions registered before the evidence arrives, a cited evidence ledger, and a confidence derived by arithmetic rather than felt. Alongside it, funnel analytics in Lab — and What's New itself.

title: Every task gets its own Claude — and goal-skill takes the build the whole way
summary: Open a task and a dedicated Claude Code session is pinned inside the task view, maintaining the document rather than implementing it. The goal orchestrator was rewritten around it — builders fork and resume, judges stay clean — plus a live agent dock, sleep that stopped duplicating knowledge, and one-click delegation from the board.
